definitions.explanation: The number one. This is the most basic counting number in Japanese. When counting objects, いち is often combined with counters like {一|いっ}つ (hitotsu), {一|いっ}{個|こ} (ikko), or {一|いち}{人|にん} (ichinin), though the pronunciation may change depending on the counter.

examples.japanese: {一|いち}から{十|じゅう}まで{数|かぞ}えてください。
examples.english: Please count from one to ten.

examples.japanese: りんごを{一|いち}つください。
{一|いち}{番|ばん}{好|す}きな{色|いろ}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What is your favorite (number one) color?

notes: The reading changes in many compound words and with different counters. For example: {一|ひと}つ (hitotsu, one thing), {一|いっ}{個|こ} (ikko, one piece), {一|いっ}{本|ぽん} (ippon, one long object). When used alone or in mathematical contexts, いち is the standard reading.
